description: The PedestrianDynamics team publishes MADRAS, a Streamlit application for exploring crowd observations from the Lyon Festival of Lights. The public app link opens and the GitHub repository offers the application code under MIT according to its own metadata; the related Zenodo snapshot lists CC BY 4.0 instead. Users can inspect flows, trajectories and interaction plots before selecting inputs for pedestrian or evacuation simulations. Coverage follows the MADRAS festival dataset, not arbitrary city-wide movement. A caveat is that the app visualizes and filters observations; it does not itself simulate pedestrian agents or guarantee that the deployed service stays available. Its code and the dataset have separate addresses. The conflicting code rights between GitHub and Zenodo need resolution before redistribution of a snapshot. I read the own app, GitHub metadata, README, Zenodo metadata and article code statement without deploying the app or downloading crowd records. No directly related catalogue record was identified.
